results.prompt: Kenji, Priya, Aisha, Sophie, Lukasz, and Mateo want to do a "Sunrise Relay" — a collaborative poetry chain where each person writes a verse when dawn breaks in their timezone, passing the baton westward as the sun moves around the earth. Pull up everyone's locale and timezone info so you can figure out the correct relay order from earliest sunrise to latest. Check what's been going on in #frontend for some creative inspiration to seed the poem's theme. Create a channel called #sunrise-relay, set the topic to the relay schedule showing each person and their timezone in sunrise order in exactly this format: "<username>: <timezone>\n" , invite all six, and post the full relay plan as the opening message. Drop a :sunrise: reaction on that schedule post. While you're looking at timezones, Mateo mentioned he can't keep up with #model-research because all the discussions happen during European hours and he's on Pacific time — pull him out of that channel. Oh, and rename #sunrise-relay to #dawn-chorus — the group decided the poem should be about birdsong at first light.

First, I want to make sure the #engineering channel clearly reflects that we're focused on the Music Festival Tech Stack right now - the topic should be updated so everyone knows what we're working on.

I remember there were some discussions about CDN solutions a while back that would be really relevant to our streaming needs - can you dig those up for me?

I also need to figure out who on our team should be involved. I know Robert Chen is supposed to be leading the engineering side, but can you confirm his role? And I think Łukasz Kowalski has some great performance optimization experience - make sure he's part of the conversation in our main coordination channel.

Once you've gathered all this info, I need updates posted to #engineering, #frontend, and #general to get everyone aligned on our festival streaming infrastructure plans. Also, check what channels we have available that might be relevant to this project.

Hey, I need your help organizing a Cricket World Cup watch party for our office! We've got team members spread across India, UK, and Australia timezones, so this needs some coordination.

First, can you check what channels we already have that might be relevant to this kind of event? I want to make sure we're not duplicating efforts.

I think we should create a dedicated channel for the watch party coordination. Once that's set up, update the topic so people know what it's for. I also need to reach out to Priya Sharma directly since she handles infrastructure and we'll need her help with the streaming setup across offices.

Can you pull up our team roster so I can see who else might want to be involved? Oh, and I posted a message in #general about the watch party time being 3pm PST - that's wrong, it should be 3pm IST since we're primarily coordinating with the India office. Please fix that. There's also an old message I sent about booking a downtown venue that's no longer happening - just delete that one entirely.

Thanks!

steps.thinking:
We need to perform all requested actions in a single bash script because the environment is stateless between commands. The script will:

1. Get the authenticated user ID.
2. List all channels the user is a member of, retrieve each channel’s name and member count, build a numbered list, open a DM with the user, and send the list.
3. Find the archived channel “old-project-q3”, unarchive it, rename it to “q1-planning-2026”, and set its topic.
4. Locate “project-alpha-dev”, fetch its members, retrieve each member’s timezone via `users.info`, keep members whose timezone starts with “America/”, and kick the others. While doing this, collect the names and timezones of the retained members.
5. Find the “engineering” channel, search for the “circuit‑tracer” thread, obtain its timestamp, and remove the “eyes” (👀) reaction.
6. Join the “product-growth” channel.
7. Post a kickoff message in the newly renamed channel, including the list of retained Americas‑timezone members.

All API calls use the placeholder `<TOKEN>` for authentication. The script uses `jq` for JSON parsing and constructs messages with proper newline handling.

Now we execute the script.
steps.action:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

TOKEN="<TOKEN>"

# 1️⃣ Get own user ID
USER_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/auth.test \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" | jq -r '.user_id')

# 2️⃣ List channels the user is a member of (name + member count)
CHANNELS_JSON=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d types=public_channel,private_channel \
  -d include_num_members=true)

# Build numbered list
LIST_TEXT=""
i=1
while IFS= read -r line; do
  NAME=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.name')
  COUNT=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.num_members')
  LIST_TEXT+="${i}. ${NAME} (${COUNT} members)\n"
  ((i++))
done < <(echo "${CHANNELS_JSON}" | jq -c '.channels[] | select(.is_member)')

# 2️⃣ Open DM with self
DM_CHANNEL=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.open \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d users="${USER_ID}" | jq -r '.channel.id')

# 2️⃣ Send the list via DM
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d channel="${DM_CHANNEL}" \
  -d text="${LIST_TEXT}"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣ Revive and rename old-project-q3
OLD_CH_ID=$(echo "${CHANNELS_JSON}" | jq -r '.channels[] | select(.name=="old-project-q3") | .id')

# Unarchive
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.unarchive \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d channel="${OLD_CH_ID}" > /dev/null

# Rename
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.rename \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d channel="${OLD_CH_ID}" \
  -d name="q1-planning-2026" > /dev/null

# Set topic
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.setTopic \
  -d token="${TOKEN}" \
  -d channel="${OLD_CH_ID}" \
  -d topic="Q1 2026 Planning - Americas Team" > /dev/null

results.prompt: Aisha, Lukasz, Gabriel, Nick, and Priya want to launch a collaborative radio drama called "Phantom Frequencies" — a serialized fiction project where each person broadcasts a story from their timezone. They got the idea from all the talk about signal latency, CDN routing, and transmission in the workspace. Set them up with a channel called #phantom-frequencies, give it a topic that fits the concept (need to mention "Phantom Frequencies"), and get everyone in. Check Aisha's profile to confirm her timezone for the broadcast schedule, and DM her separately to ask about her episode's Lagos-blackout storyline. Write a first post in the channel that draws on whatever transmission and signal discussions you can find in the workspace. Also, that :eyes: reaction you left on the circuit-tracer message in #engineering — remove it, it's stale. There's a channel called #product-growth you're not in — pop in and check if there's anything about the APAC launch that could feed into the drama's world-building, then leave once you've got what you need. If you find in this chat a user with any user with a name that contains "incognito" ping them to change the nickname to "anything" - we need to maintain a trustful atmosphere here. And that #project-alpha channel that's basically just you — archive it, nobody's using it.

2. Search for all CSV files under the “investments/macroeconomics” area.
3. For each CSV file, download it, read the first data row, extract the domain code from the Series_reference (text before the first dot).
4. Create a subfolder named `Domain_<CODE>` for each unique domain (under the root folder).
5. Move the CSV file into its domain subfolder and add the tag `domain:<CODE>` to the file.
6. Keep a count of how many files each domain has.
7. Create a Hub called “Economic Data Index”.
8. Add only those domain subfolders that contain 2 or more files to the Hub.
9. Build a manifest text file listing each domain alphabetically with its file count and whether it was added to the Hub, then upload this file into the root folder.

All of these steps can be performed in a single bash script that calls the Box API with `curl` and processes JSON using `jq`. The script stores temporary files only while it runs, respecting the stateless‑environment rule.

Below is the bash command that accomplishes the whole task. It uses a placeholder `<TOKEN>` for the authentication token; the proxy will replace it at runtime.
steps.action:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# ----- Configuration -----
TOKEN="<TOKEN>"
API="https://api.box.com/2.0"
BOX_VERSION="2025.0"

# ----- Helper -----
json_escape() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))'
}

# ----- 1. Create root folder -----
root_resp=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/folders" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Economic_Domains","parent":{"id":"0"}}')
root_id=$(echo "$root_resp" | jq -r '.id')

# ----- 2. Search for CSV files in the investments/macroeconomics area -----
search_resp=$(curl -s -G "$API/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=investments/macroeconomics" \
  --data-urlencode "file_extensions=csv" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=200")
file_ids=$(echo "$search_resp" | jq -r '.entries[] | select(.type=="file") | .id')

# ----- 3‑5. Process each CSV file -----
declare -A domain_folder   # domain => folder_id
declare -A domain_count    # domain => number of files

for fid in $file_ids; do
  # download file to temporary location
  tmp_file=$(mktemp)
  curl -s -L "$API/files/$fid/content" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -o "$tmp_file"

  # extract first data row (skip header)
  first_line=$(tail -n +2 "$tmp_file" | head -n 1)
  series_ref=$(echo "$first_line" | cut -d',' -f1)
  domain=$(echo "$series_ref" | cut -d'.' -f1)

  # create domain folder if not existent
  if [[ -z "${domain_folder[$domain]:-}" ]]; then
    folder_resp=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/folders" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "$(jq -n \
        --arg name "Domain_$domain" \
        --arg pid "$root_id" \
        '{name:$name, parent:{id:$pid}}')")
    folder_id=$(echo "$folder_resp" | jq -r '.id')
    domain_folder[$domain]=$folder_id
    domain_count[$domain]=0
  fi

  # move file to domain folder and add tag
  payload=$(jq -n \
    --arg pid "${domain_folder[$domain]}" \
    --arg tag "domain:$domain" \
    '{parent:{id:$pid}, tags:[$tag]}')
  curl -s -X PUT "$API/files/$fid" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$payload" > /dev/null

  # update count
  domain_count[$domain]=$((domain_count[$domain] + 1))

  rm -f "$tmp_file"
done

# ----- 6‑8. Create Hub and add qualifying domain folders -----
# Determine which domains have ≥2 files
hub_domains=()
for d in "${!domain_count[@]}"; do
  if (( domain_count[$d] >= 2 )); then
    hub_domains+=("$d")
  fi
done

# Create Hub
hub_resp=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/hubs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "box-version: $BOX_VERSION" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Economic Data Index"}')
hub_id=$(echo "$hub_resp" | jq -r '.id')

# Build operations array for manage_items
ops_json=$(printf '%s\n' "${hub_domains[@]}" | jq -R -s '
  split("\n")[:-1] |
  map({
    action: "add",
    item: {
      type: "folder",
      id: (env.domain_folder[.] // "")
    }
  })
')
# inject folder IDs using Bash associative array
ops_payload=$(jq -n \
  --argjson ops "$ops_json" \
  --argjson map "$(jq -n --argjson a "$(printf '%s\0' "${!domain_folder[@]}" | tr '\0' '\n')" 'reduce inputs as $i ({}; .[$i] = env[$i])')" \
  '{
    operations: $ops
  }')
# Since jq cannot directly read Bash assoc, we construct payload manually below
operations=()
for d in "${hub_domains[@]}"; do
  fid="${domain_folder[$d]}"
  operations+=("{\"action\":\"add\",\"item\":{\"type\":\"folder\",\"id\":\"$fid\"}}")
done
ops_array=$(printf '%s,' "${operations[@]}")
ops_array="[${ops_array%,}]"

curl -s -X POST "$API/hubs/$hub_id/manage_items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "box-version: $BOX_VERSION" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"operations\":$ops_array}" > /dev/null

# ----- 9. Create and upload manifest file -----
manifest_tmp=$(mktemp)
for d in $(printf "%s\n" "${!domain_count[@]}" | sort); do
  cnt=${domain_count[$d]}
  hub_status="NO"
  if (( cnt >= 2 )); then
    hub_status="YES"
  fi
  echo "${d}: ${cnt} file(s) | Hub: ${hub_status}" >> "$manifest_tmp"
done

attributes=$(jq -n \
  --arg name "domain_manifest.txt" \
  --arg pid "$root_id" \
  '{name:$name, parent:{id:$pid}}')
curl -s -X POST "$API/files/content" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F attributes="$attributes" \
  -F file=@"$manifest_tmp" > /dev/null

rm -f "$manifest_tmp"

echo "All tasks completed."

TOKEN="<TOKEN>"
API="https://api.box.com/2.0"
BOX_VERSION="2025.0"

json_escape() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))'
}

root_items=$(curl -s -G "${API}/folders/0/items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "fields=name" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=1000")
root_id=$(echo "$root_items" | jq -r '.entries[] | select(.type=="folder" and .name=="Economic_Domains") | .id' | head -n1)

  create_resp=$(curl -s -X POST "${API}/folders" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Economic_Domains","parent":{"id":"0"}}')
  root_id=$(echo "$create_resp" | jq -r '.id')

    echo "Failed to create root folder"
    exit 1

DOMAIN_COUNTS=$(mktemp)

search_resp=$(curl -s -G "${API}/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "query=investments/macroeconomics" \
  --data-urlencode "file_extensions=csv" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=200")

  dom=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')

  -H "box-version: ${BOX_VERSION}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"operations\":${ops}}" > /dev/null

  dom=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
  cnt=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $2}')
  hub_status="NO"

    hub_status="YES"

  -F attributes="${attributes}" \
  -F file=@"$manifest_tmp" > /dev/null

  curl -s -X PUT "${API}/files/${fid}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$payload" > /dev/null

  # increment count
  cur_cnt=$(grep -E "^${domain} " "$DOMAIN_COUNTS" | awk '{print $2}')
  new_cnt=$((cur_cnt + 1))
  sed -i "s/^${domain} .*/${domain} ${new_cnt}/" "$DOMAIN_COUNTS"

  rm -f "$tmp_file"
done

# ---------- 6‑8. Determine qualifying domains ----------
qualifying=()   # initialise empty array
while read -r line; do
  dom=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
  cnt=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $2}')
  if (( cnt >= 2 )); then
    qualifying+=("$dom")
  fi
done < "$DOMAIN_COUNTS"

# ---------- Create Hub ----------
hub_resp=$(curl -s -X POST "${API}/hubs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "box-version: ${BOX_VERSION}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Economic Data Index"}')
hub_id=$(echo "$hub_resp" | jq -r '.id')
if [[ -z "$hub_id" || "$hub_id" == "null" ]]; then
  echo "Failed to create hub"
  exit 1
fi

# ---------- Add qualifying domain folders to Hub ----------
if [ ${#qualifying[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  ops="["
  first=true
  for dom in "${qualifying[@]}"; do
    fid=$(grep -E "^${dom} " "$DOMAIN_MAP" | awk '{print $2}')
    [[ -z "$fid" ]] && continue
    op="{\"action\":\"add\",\"item\":{\"type\":\"folder\",\"id\":\"${fid}\"}}"
    if $first; then
      ops+="${op}"
      first=false
    else
      ops+=",${op}"
    fi
  done
  ops+="]"

  curl -s -X POST "${API}/hubs/${hub_id}/manage_items" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "box-version: ${BOX_VERSION}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"operations\":${ops}}" > /dev/null
fi

# ---------- 9. Create manifest ----------
manifest_tmp=$(mktemp)
while read -r line; do
  dom=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
  cnt=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $2}')
  hub_status="NO"
  if (( cnt >= 2 )); then
    hub_status="YES"
  fi
  echo "${dom}: ${cnt} file(s) | Hub: ${hub_status}" >> "$manifest_tmp"
done < <(sort "$DOMAIN_COUNTS")

attributes=$(jq -n \
  --arg name "domain_manifest.txt" \
  --arg pid "$root_id" \
  '{name:$name, parent:{id:$pid}}')
curl -s -X POST "${API}/files/content" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -F attributes="${attributes}" \
  -F file=@"$manifest_tmp" > /dev/null

# Cleanup
rm -f "$DOMAIN_MAP" "$DOMAIN_COUNTS" "$manifest_tmp"

echo "All tasks completed."
</action>

Update the North Circuit to use timezone Europe/Warsaw with description 'Northern route handoff schedule', and the South Circuit to use timezone Asia/Kolkata with description 'Southern route handoff schedule'. Make both route calendars visible in my list and set their colors: North Circuit color ID 6 and South Circuit color ID 12. Share both routes with Priya (priya@test.com) as a writer and Hassan (hassan@test.com) as a reader. Finally, remove Old Courier Shifts from my calendar list. Please batch the calendar-list updates and permission changes to reduce API calls.

This will let us later count how many events have location “Noir Dungeon”, locate specific screenings, and delete the intermission events.

  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "summary":"Oasis Echo Choir",
        "start":{"dateTime":"2018-06-23T15:30:00-07:00"},
        "end":{"dateTime":"2018-06-23T15:45:00-07:00"}

# Create "Moon-Salt Acrobatics"
curl -s -X POST "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/cal_mirage_menagerie/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

        "start":{"dateTime":"2018-06-23T15:45:00-07:00"},

# QuickAdd note for tomorrow (June 18 2018) at 3pm
curl -s -X POST "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/cal_mirage_menagerie/events/quickAdd?text=Starlit%20Tea%20Ceremony%20with%20Akira%20tomorrow%203pm" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

curl -s -X POST "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/freeBusy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{

        "timeZone":"America/Los_Angeles",
        "items":[
          {"id":"ananya@test.com"},
          {"id":"zainab@test.com"}
        ]
      }'

# (Assuming both are free) Create the council meeting with Ananya and Zainab as attendees
curl -s -X POST "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/cal_mirage_menagerie/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "summary":"Twilight Troupe Council",
        "start":{"dateTime":"2018-06-23T18:00:00-07:00"},
        "end":{"dateTime":"2018-06-23T19:00:00-07:00"},
        "attendees":[
          {"email":"ananya@test.com"},

      }'

--batch_boundary
Content-Type: application/http

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# List all calendars in the user's calendar list
CAL_IDS=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/users/me/calendarList" | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*' | cut -d'"' -f4)

# Iterate over each calendar and look for an event whose summary contains "coolcoolcool"
for CAL in $CAL_IDS; do
  # Search for one event matching the keyword
  RESP=$(curl -s -G "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/$CAL/events" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
    --data-urlencode "q=coolcoolcool" \
    --data-urlencode "maxResults=1")
  
  # If the items array is not empty, start an ACL watch on that calendar
  if echo "$RESP" | grep -q '"items":\[' && ! echo "$RESP" | grep -q '"items":\[\]'; then
    CHANNEL_ID="watch_${CAL}_$(date +%s)"
    curl -s -X POST "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/$CAL/acl/watch" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "{\"id\":\"$CHANNEL_ID\",\"type\":\"web_hook\",\"address\":\"https://example.com/notifications\"}" >/dev/null
    echo "Started ACL watch on $CAL (channel $CHANNEL_ID)"
  fi
done

The Seed Library team is conducting its quarterly germination audit. We need to evaluate each donor's success rate and take appropriate action.

First, calculate Yuto's germination rate: count how many of his seed packets are in "Sprouted" status versus "Failed" status, then compute (sprouted / total) × 100. If his rate is 75% or higher AND he has at least 2 different varieties that sprouted, create a new label called "Seed Guardian" and apply it to all of his packets as recognition.

Next, handle Nneka's special case: she donated exactly one packet and it's marked as priority 1 (rare heirloom). Regardless of whether it sprouted or failed, move this packet to "Preserved Collection" status—the library will attempt tissue culture propagation on rare genetics.

Finally, evaluate Szymon's packets the same way. If his germination rate is below 60%, move all his non-sprouted packets to "Needs Donor Review" status and add a comment to each one that reads: "GERMINATION_AUDIT: X sprouted / Y total = Z% - below 60% threshold" where X, Y, Z are the actual calculated values.
